subject: tech
title: Lights, Buzzers and Motors
about: The outputs electricity can drive: a tiny light (LED) glows, a buzzer makes a sound, a motor spins fan blades or toy car wheels, a tiny motor makes a tablet buzz, and a screen is many tiny lights; a sensor is an input, each output has its own switch, more electricity means brighter or faster up to a point, and a motor empties a battery faster than a tiny light. Electricity is a bridge topic (NC science teaches it in Grade 4), tagged to K2-CS-02 (what hardware parts do), and it follows Circuits and Switches (the loop) and In and Out (computer parts) without repeating them. Read it together with a flashlight, a battery toy and a fan in reach.
tip: Hunt for outputs around the house: point at each thing and ask, does it make light, sound or movement?

cards.q: A light, a buzzer and a motor each do something when electricity flows in. What do we call them?
cards.note: Light, sound and movement are outputs, the things electricity comes out as. A sensor or a button is an input.

cards.q: A light sensor notices the dark and a lamp turns on. Which part is the output?
cards.note: The sensor notices, so it is the input. The lamp does something you can see, so it is the output.

cards.q: The tiny glowing light on a charger or a toy has a three-letter name. What is it?
cards.note: L E D is a tiny light that glows with very little electricity. Count the LEDs on your charger and toys.

cards.q: A doorbell needs to make a sound when you press it. Which part does the job?
cards.note: A buzzer turns electricity into sound. Press the button and it buzzes or rings.

cards.q: A night-light needs a soft glow all night. Which part does the job?
cards.note: A tiny light gives a soft glow and uses very little electricity, so it can stay on all night.

cards.q: A fan needs to spin its blades. Which part does the job?
cards.note: A motor turns electricity into spinning. Fans, toy cars and blenders all have one.

cards.q: A motor gets electricity. Which kind of output does it make?
cards.note: A motor turns electricity into movement: spinning wheels, fan blades, a wiggling toothbrush. A tiny light makes light and a buzzer makes sound.

cards.q: A clock must make a loud sound to wake you up. Which part do you pick?
cards.note: A buzzer makes the loud sound. A tiny light could not wake you, and a motor would just spin.

cards.q: You press the doorbell button and the buzzer sounds. What kind of part is the button?
cards.note: The button is a switch. It is the input that closes the loop, and the buzzer is the output.

cards.q: The tablet buzzes in your pocket. What tiny part is spinning inside to make the buzz?
cards.note: A tiny motor with a lopsided weight spins fast, and that makes the buzz you feel. It is called a vibration motor.

cards.q: A screen lights up with a picture. What makes the glow?
cards.note: A screen is made of many, many tiny lights that change color. Together they make the picture.

cards.q: A tiny light gets a little more electricity. What happens?
cards.note: More electricity, brighter light, up to a point. Every light has a limit.

cards.q: A grown-up puts a second battery in a toy car. What does the motor do?
cards.note: Two batteries push harder, so the motor spins faster. Only use as many as the toy is made for.

cards.q: A tiny light gets way too much electricity. What can happen?
cards.note: Too much electricity and a light burns out. Toys are made to give each part just the right amount.

cards.q: A toy has a light and a buzzer, each with its own switch. You flip only the light switch. What turns on?
cards.note: Each output can have its own switch. Flip one switch, and only that part gets electricity.

cards.q: A toy runs on one small battery. Which part empties the battery the fastest?
cards.note: A motor pulls a lot of electricity to spin, but a tiny light only sips. Motor toys need new batteries sooner.

cards.q: Why can a tiny light glow all night on one small battery?
cards.note: A tiny light uses very little electricity, so one small battery lasts a long, long time.

cards.q: An electric toothbrush wiggles back and forth. What is inside making it move?
cards.note: A small motor spins inside the handle and makes the brush wiggle. Motors are everywhere!
